extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and peer reviewers who review for Cambridge University Press journals
extracted.subtask_short: using Web of Science reviewer recognition
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Cambridge reviewers on claiming, recording, and showcasing peer-review contributions via the Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service (formerly Publons), while preserving reviewer anonymity and complying with journal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web of Science Researcher Profile purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Web of Science's researcher profile helps you to record, verify, and showcase your peer review contributions for use in promotion applications. You get recognition even if your reviews are anonymous and the manuscript is never published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you submit a review to a partner journal, you will be given the option to get recognition for your review on the Web of Science. You will be directed to create a profile to which your review is added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and display policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service gives recognition for peer review without compromising reviewer anonymity or infringing upon journal policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default, the content of the review will not be publicly displayed, and only the year of the review and the journal title will be shown on reviewer profiles. You may edit what is displayed for any review or opt out of the service at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals integration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only reviews for journals integrated with the Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service can be added via the automatic/partner workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The majority of Cambridge's ScholarOne titles are integrated with the service, alongside a select number of journals using Editorial Manager. Integration status determines whether you are asked/offered recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming a review (process)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing for an integrated journal you will be asked if you want to get recognition for the review; once the review is completed you will receive an email with a private link to claim the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the private link in the email to add your review to your researcher profile. This is the recommended workflow for adding individual reviews securely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic addition option for future reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: You can elect to have all future reviews you complete for the journal automatically added to your profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming a review (or when prompted during submission), you may choose an option to automatically add subsequent reviews for that journal to your Web of Science profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of recording reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording reviews provides a free way to track, verify and showcase your peer review activities, creating an online record of your contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This record can be used as evidence of disciplinary expertise in job applications, performance evaluations and funding applications; Cambridge highlights that the service offers a quick and easy way to link reviews you do for them to your researcher profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting started (account creation)
rubrics_metrics.description: To use the Reviewer Recognition Service you need a Web of Science researcher profile/account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can create a free account to get a head start on your reviewer profile and view example researcher profiles to learn more.
